Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). ## claude.ai Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. # Brief

## The Task
### Background
A recruiter user will provide their search inputs at `data\user_search_inputs`, which are:
- Companies they wish to search the career pages of e.g. Deloitte
- Job titles they wish to search for e.g. Senior Consultant
- Locations they wish to find these roles e.g. United Kingdom

### The Task
This task is matching 1,500 real mass-scraped jobs at `data\jobs_raw.jsonl` to these search inputs. This process is downstream of the career page scraping process, all data provided is local & you are **not** expected to perform any live searches.

We have provided a version 1 located at `v1\workers\job_matcher`, which provides a basic framework to start from, however it is deliberately broken & does not match jobs accurately. See the README for a deeper understanding.

Recruiters are paid a % fee, from 15-30% of a salary, meaning sending a £100K salary Candidate to an open role & then being hired, earning a Recruitment company £15-£30K. Recruitment is critically based off speed, Career Pages are typically the first place a job goes live before hitting job boards such as LinkedIn, Indeed, Reed etc, meaning if we can successfully scrape career pages & filter accurately, this can create strong leads for Recruiters.

### What we're looking for
This task is to create a successfully matching codebase that matches our production job_matcher answers to within 90%, on a dataset we hold privately.

More importantly, we're assessing how you get there:
- Clear, concise code: a small, well-scoped solution with clear trade-offs is better than a big one.
- Efficiency: think about time and space complexity, it must run 200k jobs in under 20 minutes.
- Well-written tests for the rules & logic you implement.
- Your process: commit little and often, it's important for us to see a timeline

We expect AI-assisted coding tools will be used, but make sure PLAN.md, DECISIONS.md & NOTES.md are concisely written documents.


## The Build
### Matching standards
- The matching is pass / fail. A job goes in only when all three match: the company, at least one job title, at least one location.
- Precision matters more than volume, the core selling point of this product is it doesn't produce noise.
- A job in several places is in if ANY of them matches: "Bristol, Manchester" for a recruiter with "Bristol" in their search inputs, this is a pass.
- The company must appear somewhere on the job page (declared company, heading, title tag, URL or body text). That's only a loose validator to ensure we have the correct career page, because the search upstream should have already picked the correct company's career page.
- A recruiter needs evidence the job is live. A dead link (404 / 410) never goes in.
- Full definitions: [OUTPUT_FORMAT.json](OUTPUT_FORMAT.json).


### Engineering preferences
- An LLM API will be provided before the task, see the example at .env.example. These are live API calls from API keys with capped budgets & there will likely be cases where an LLM is required, you should aim for £1 target, £3 max spend.
- The use of LLM matching should be at your discretion, although keep in mind the cost vs matching via code.
- It must run on 200k jobs in under 20 minutes.
- `tools/make_scale_feed.py` builds the 200,000-job test feed from `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`.
- No scraping happens, each job already carries the page we fetched once (`page.http_status` + what it showed). Blocked pages, dead links, blank locations, title mismatches, wrong company on the page. Japanese-script locations and "3 Locations" placeholders are all in that data. Each needs a defensible policy.

### The 4 phases
Plan     - 15-30 minutes - `PLAN.md`, handwritten documents 
Build    - 15-30 minutes - commits
Tune     - 15-30 minutes - commits
Complete - 15-30 minutes - `NOTES.md`

1-2 hours total (self-timed), there are no bonus points for exceeding the time limit. Log your start and end in `NOTES.md`, log every decision in `DECISIONS.md` as you make it.

Commit little and often, at every step, not once at the end, we want to see the development of commits over a timeline.


## Your inputs
All inputs live in `data\`.

### Search inputs
Each recruiter has a folder at `data\user_search_inputs\`, e.g. `profile_a`, holding the three searches they set up:
`company_searches.json` lists the companies they recruit for (the industry field is context only & about half filled)
`job_title_searches.json` lists the job titles they place
`location_searches.json` lists where they work, with every location carrying a name, a country, a type & an `includes` list of the towns it covers.

A `city` covers its own name & its includes, a `sub_region` (a region, nation or county) also covers any town inside it, and `remote` covers jobs the employer says are remote or home-based in that country, but a job in another country is never inside a location, whatever the town is called.

Every file carries the same `profile_id`, which goes on every output line, and the starter reads the folder back into one profile for you through `load_search_inputs` in `v1\shared\patterns\worker_runtime.py`. We grade on a different recruiter's folder, so nothing should be hard-coded to `profile_a`.

### The jobs
`data\jobs_raw.jsonl` holds about 1,500 jobs, one per line. Each has a `job_id` to copy to your output unchanged, the `scraped` fields our scraper stored (title, company, location & salary, which are often abbreviated, blank or wrong), the `source_url` it was found at (anonymised, so it will not load), and the `page` exactly as we fetched it once: its `http_status`, then whatever it showed, which is the title tag, the h1, the meta tags, the visible text and `structured_job`, the job facts the page declared itself (title, company & locations). Any of these can be missing or empty.

### Answers & tests
`data\labelled_sample.jsonl` has 60 jobs with the right decision, matched company, job titles & locations, and reason, and is the only answer key you get. `data\golden\` holds a tiny feed & profile the starter already passes, which `make test` runs.

# job_matcher worker (v1)

This version is deliberately incorrect and error-ridden, run it with `make run`
(`python -m v1.workers.job_matcher.handler [--jobs ...] [--search-inputs ...]`).

The worker framework looks like this:
- `v1/shared` - the global shared code (runtime, logging, `sli_observe`, schemas, `llm.py`)
- `v1/workers` - one folder per worker, these would typically be AWS Fargate workers in production
- `handler.py` - the entry point
- `stages` - the 2 core steps, cleaning the data (`stage_clean_jobs`) then matching it (`stage_match_jobs`)
- `modules` - the python files that each stage runs, in its `STAGE_GRAPH` order
- `_shared` - helpers only this specific worker uses, e.g. `town_lookup.py`

## What a run writes (`runs/<trace_id>/`)

- `profile_<id>_matched.jsonl` - the output
- `sli_events.jsonl` - one fact per row per module (outcome, reason), shows where rows died
- `llm_calls.jsonl` - every LLM call, with its cost and purpose

## Module contract

Follow this for any module you add or change.

Constants at the top: `MODULE_NAME`, `MODULE_TYPE` (transform / filter / explode), `REJECTION_REASONS`,
`ERROR_REASONS` and `WARNING_REASONS`.

`main(context, prev_data)` opens with `trace_id`, `start_time` and `logger`, tags every row
(`reject(row, "REASON")` or leave it "pass"), calls `sli_observe` once at the end on all rows, and returns one
`ExecutionResult`. No `print()`, no row totals in logs.

You may restructure it however you like. In this shape, a new step is a new file in `modules/` plus one
`StageDefinition` in a stage's `STAGE_GRAPH`.

    location_searches.json {"profile_id", "locations"}, read back into one profile. A missing file or a
    profile_id that differs between the three raises. A plain <prefix>.json profile (the older layout) still loads."""
    profiles: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
    for folder in sorted(p for p in root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
        present = {field: folder / name for field, name in SEARCH_INPUT_FILES.items() if (folder / name).exists()}
        if not present:
            continue
        if len(present) != len(SEARCH_INPUT_FILES):
            missing = sorted(set(SEARCH_INPUT_FILES.values()) - {p.name for p in present.values()})
            raise ValueError(f"{folder}: missing search input files {missing}")
        parts = {field: json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) for field, path in present.items()}
        ids = {part["profile_id"] for part in parts.values()}
        if len(ids) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{folder}: profile_id differs across the search input files: {sorted(ids)}")
        profiles.append((folder.name, {"profile_id": ids.pop(), **{f: parts[f][f] for f in SEARCH_INPUT_FILES}}))
    for path in sorted(root.glob("*.json")):
        profiles.append((path.stem, json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))))
    return profiles


def run_pipeline(
    stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition],
    input_schema: dict,
    output_schema: dict,
    handler_name: str,
    jobs_path: Path,
    search_inputs_dir: Path,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """One trace per call; one "message" per recruiter in search_inputs_dir. Returns {output file: listed job count}."""
    trace_id = new_trace_id()
    logger = get_logger(handler_name)
    llm.start_run(run_dir(trace_id))
    log_event(logger, "info", "run_started", trace_id, jobs_path=str(jobs_path),
              search_inputs_dir=str(search_inputs_dir))  # fmt: skip
    outputs: dict[str, str] = {}
    for prefix, profile in load_search_inputs(Path(search_inputs_dir)):
        context = {
            "trace_id": trace_id,
            "jobs_path": str(jobs_path),
            "profile": profile,
            "profile_id": profile["profile_id"],
            "output_prefix": prefix,
        }
        validate_context(context, input_schema)
        data: list[dict] = []
        for node in stage_graph.values():
            result = importlib.import_module(node.module_path).main(context, data)
            data = result.data
            context.update(result.artifacts)
        validate_context(context, output_schema)
        outputs[context["output_path"]] = str(len(data))
    log_event(logger, "info", "run_finished", trace_id, outputs=outputs, llm_spent_gbp=round(llm.spent_gbp(), 4))
    return outputs


def run_local_handler(
    stage_graph: dict[str, StageDefinition], input_schema: dict, output_schema: dict, handler_name: str
) -> int:
    """Entry point for `python -m <handler module>`: parse --jobs / --search-inputs, run, print one line per output."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=handler_name)
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_JOBS)
    parser.add_argument("--search-inputs", "--briefs", dest="search_inputs", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SEARCH_INPUTS)
    args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
    for path, count in run_pipeline(
        stage_graph, input_schema, output_schema, handler_name, args.jobs, args.search_inputs
    ).items():
        print(f"{count:>5} matches -> {path}")
    return 0

"""Keep the jobs that fit one recruiter profile: a listed company, a profile title, a profile location."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from v1.shared.observability.sli_observe import passed, reject, sli_observe
from v1.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v1.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult, debug_limits
from v1.workers.job_matcher._shared.town_lookup import towns_covered

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__match_jobs"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"COMPANY_NOT_LISTED", "NO_TITLE_MATCH", "NO_LOCATION_MATCH"}
ERROR_REASONS: set[str] = set()
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()


def matched_titles(job_title: str, titles: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Profile titles that appear in the job title."""
    return [t for t in titles if t in job_title]


def matched_locations(town: str, locations: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    """Profile locations whose town list holds the job's town."""
    return [loc["name"] for loc in locations if town in towns_covered(loc)]


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Filter the located jobs down to context["profile"]; each match carries what it matched."""
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)
    debug_mode, debug_loops = debug_limits()
    profile = context["profile"]
    companies = {c["name"] for c in profile["companies"]}

    # ==================================================================
    # L1: Test every job against the profile (on a copy: the same jobs feed every profile)
    # ==================================================================
    rows = [dict(r) for r in prev_data]
    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
        if debug_mode and i >= debug_loops:
            log_event(logger, "debug", "debug_mode_stop", trace_id, stopped_at=i)
            break
        if row["company"] not in companies:
            reject(row, "COMPANY_NOT_LISTED")
            continue
        titles = matched_titles(row["title"], profile["titles"])
        if not titles:
            reject(row, "NO_TITLE_MATCH")
            continue
        locations = matched_locations(row["town"], profile["locations"])
        if not locations:
            reject(row, "NO_LOCATION_MATCH")
            continue
        row["matched_company"] = row["company"]
        row["matched_job_title"] = titles
        row["matched_location"] = locations
        row["reason"] = f"{row['title']} at {row['company']}, in {row['town']}"

    # ==================================================================
    # L2: Record outcomes, hand on the matches
    # ==================================================================
    kept = passed(rows)
    log_event(logger, "info", "match_jobs_done", trace_id, profile_id=profile["profile_id"])
    sli_observe(rows, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id, script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}", data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={}
    )

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path

BUDGET_GBP = 3.00  # hard stop; the task budget is £1 (spend above it is questioned)
USD_TO_GBP = 0.79
DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 500

}

_run_dir: Path | None = None
_clients: dict[str, object] = {}


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):

def start_run(run_dir: Path) -> None:
    """Called by the handler: this run's calls are logged in run_dir/llm_calls.jsonl."""

    return Path(os.environ.get("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", "runs"))

    """Total spend so far, across every run folder."""
    total = 0.0

def _send(name: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int, schema: dict | None) -> tuple[str, int, int, str]:
    """One provider call -> (text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, stop_reason)."""
    spec = PROVIDERS[name]
    if name == "anthropic":
        import anthropic

        client = _clients.setdefault(name, anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=os.environ[spec["key"]]))
        output_config: dict = {"effort": "low"}
        if schema:
            output_config["format"] = {"type": "json_schema", "schema": schema}
        response = client.messages.create(
            model=spec["model"],
            max_tokens=max_tokens,
            output_config=output_config,
            messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        )
        text = "".join(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text")
        return text, response.usage.input_tokens, response.usage.output_tokens, str(response.stop_reason)
    from google import genai
    from google.genai import types

    client = _clients.setdefault(name, genai.Client(api_key=os.environ[spec["key"]]))
    config = types.GenerateContentConfig(
        max_output_tokens=max_tokens,
        temperature=0.0,
        thinking_config=types.ThinkingConfig(thinking_budget=0),
        **({"response_mime_type": "application/json", "response_json_schema": schema} if schema else {}),
    )
    response = client.models.generate_content(model=spec["model"], contents=prompt, config=config)
    usage = response.usage_metadata
    completion = (usage.candidates_token_count or 0) + (usage.thoughts_token_count or 0)
    finish = response.candidates[0].finish_reason if response.candidates else None
    return response.text or "", usage.prompt_token_count or 0, completion, str(finish)


def _call(prompt: str, max_tokens: int, purpose: str, schema: dict | None) -> str:
    name = provider()
    total = _guard(name, prompt, max_tokens)
    started = time.time()
    text, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, stop_reason = _send(name, prompt, max_tokens, schema)
    cost = cost_gbp(name, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens)
    run_dir = _run_dir or (_runs_root() / time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S", time.gmtime(started)))
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with (run_dir / "llm_calls.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "ts": round(started, 3),
                    "provider": name,
                    "model": PROVIDERS[name]["model"],
                    "purpose": purpose,
                    "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens,
                    "completion_tokens": completion_tokens,
                    "cost_gbp": round(cost, 6),
                    "total_gbp": round(total + cost, 6),
                    "stop_reason": stop_reason,
                    "latency_ms": round((time.time() - started) * 1000),

    """Send one prompt, get the text reply. `purpose` is logged so the spend can be read back."""
    return _call(prompt, max_tokens, purpose, None)

    return json.loads(_call(prompt, max_tokens, purpose, schema))

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from v1.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import run_pipeline
from v1.workers.job_matcher import handler

GOLDEN = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "data" / "golden"
REQUIRED = {"job_id", "profile_id", "matched_company", "matched_job_title", "matched_location", "reason", "used_llm"}


def test_golden_feed_matches_listed_company_title_and_town(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("ILLUMINI_RUNS_DIR", str(tmp_path))
    outputs = run_pipeline(
        handler.STAGE_GRAPH,
        handler.INPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.OUTPUT_CONTEXT_SCHEMA,
        handler.HANDLER_NAME,
        GOLDEN / "jobs_small.jsonl",
        GOLDEN / "user_search_inputs",
    )
    ((path, count),) = outputs.items()
    rows = {r["job_id"]: r for r in map(json.loads, Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines())}
    assert Path(path).name == "profile_golden_matched.jsonl" and count == "2"
    assert set(rows) == {"G000001", "G000002"}
    assert rows["G000001"]["matched_company"] == "Golden Fixture Ltd"
    assert rows["G000001"]["matched_job_title"] == ["Controls Engineer"]
    assert rows["G000001"]["matched_location"] == ["Warrington"]
    for row in rows.values():
        assert REQUIRED <= row.keys()
        assert row["profile_id"] == "golden" and row["matched_job_title"] and row["matched_location"] and row["reason"]

"""Resolve each job's location string to a known UK town and region."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from v1.shared.observability.sli_observe import passed, reject, sli_observe
from v1.shared.patterns.logging import get_logger, log_event
from v1.shared.patterns.worker_runtime import ExecutionResult, debug_limits
from v1.workers.job_matcher._shared.town_lookup import lookup_town

MODULE_NAME = "job_matcher__resolve_job_town"
MODULE_TYPE = "filter"
REJECTION_REASONS = {"UNKNOWN_LOCATION"}
ERROR_REASONS: set[str] = set()
WARNING_REASONS: set[str] = set()


def main(context: dict, prev_data: list[dict]) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Tag each row with town / region / country; rows we cannot place are rejected UNKNOWN_LOCATION."""
    trace_id: str = context.get("trace_id")
    start_time = time.time()
    logger = get_logger(MODULE_NAME)
    debug_mode, debug_loops = debug_limits()

    # ==================================================================
    # L1: Look up every location
    # ==================================================================
    for i, row in enumerate(prev_data):
        if debug_mode and i >= debug_loops:
            log_event(logger, "debug", "debug_mode_stop", trace_id, stopped_at=i)
            break
        place = lookup_town(row["location"])
        if place is None:
            reject(row, "UNKNOWN_LOCATION")
            continue
        row.update(town=place["town"], region=place["region"], country=place["country"], used_llm=False)

    # ==================================================================
    # L2: Record outcomes, hand on the placed rows
    # ==================================================================
    kept = passed(prev_data)
    log_event(logger, "info", "resolve_job_town_done", trace_id)
    sli_observe(prev_data, MODULE_NAME, start_time, trace_id)
    return ExecutionResult(
        trace_id=trace_id, script_span_id=f"{MODULE_NAME}_{trace_id}", data=kept, artifacts={}, metrics={}
    )

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Commands

```bash
make dev          # create venv, install deps (incl. dev), install pre-commit hooks
make run          # run the job_matcher on the real feed; writes runs/<timestamp>/profile_a_matched.jsonl
make test         # run the full pytest suite (golden + llm_cap tests)

# Single test
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_golden.py -q

# Debug mode (stops each module after 5 rows)
DEBUG_MODE=true make run

# Scale feed (200k jobs from the 1.5k raw)
.venv/bin/python tools/make_scale_feed.py
```

The `.env` file must have `ANTHROPIC_SENIOR_DEVELOPER_KEY` or `GEMINI_SENIOR_DEVELOPER_KEY`. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`.

## Architecture

This is a **two-stage pipeline** with a strict module contract. The entry point is `v1/workers/job_matcher/handler.py`, which defines a `STAGE_GRAPH` of two stages:

1. **`stage_clean_jobs`** — load, normalise, dedup, and resolve the raw job feed to a canonical shape
2. **`stage_match_jobs`** — filter jobs against one recruiter profile; write the output file

Each stage itself has a `STAGE_GRAPH` of **modules** run in order. The data flows: `handler → stage → module → module → ...` Each step receives `context` (a dict with the run's metadata/profile) and `prev_data` (list of row dicts), and returns an `ExecutionResult`. Stages are in `stages/`, modules are in `modules/`.

### Module contract (must be followed for all new/changed modules)

- Top-level constants: `MODULE_NAME`, `MODULE_TYPE` (`transform`/`filter`/`explode`), `REJECTION_REASONS`, `ERROR_REASONS`, `WARNING_REASONS`
- `main(context, prev_data) -> ExecutionResult`
- Tag each row with `reject(row, "REASON")` from `sli_observe`; call `sli_observe(rows, ...)` **once** at the end on **all** rows (not just kept ones)
- Return `ExecutionResult(..., data=kept)` where `kept = passed(rows)`
- No `print()`. Use `log_event(logger, ...)` from `v1/shared/patterns/logging.py`

### Observability

Every run writes to `runs/<trace_id>/`:
- `profile_<id>_matched.jsonl` — the output (one JSON line per matched job)
- `sli_events.jsonl` — one event per row per module (outcome, rejection reason); use this to diagnose where rows are dropped
- `llm_calls.jsonl` — every LLM call with tokens and GBP cost

### LLM usage

`v1/shared/api_calls/llm.py` is the **only** way to call an LLM. Use `ask(prompt, purpose=...)` for text or `ask_json(prompt, schema=..., purpose=...)` for structured output. Budget: £1 target, £3.00 hard stop (`BudgetExceeded` raised before sending). Provider: Anthropic if its key is set, else Gemini.

## Matching rules (from OUTPUT_FORMAT.json)

A job is included when **all three** pass:

| Signal | Rule |
|--------|------|
| **Company** | Company name appears anywhere on the page (declared fields, title tag, URL, body text). Match ignores case, punctuation, a leading "The", and legal suffixes (Ltd, plc, Group, Holdings, International, UK). |
| **Title** | Every word of the profile title appears in the job's title in any order, case/punctuation-insensitive, ignoring a trailing plural *s*. |
| **Location** | A `city` covers itself + its `includes`. A `sub_region` covers itself + any town inside it. A `remote` location covers jobs the employer declares remote/home-based in that country. Multiple locations on a job: match if **any** matches. Jobs in a different country never match. |
| **Live** | HTTP status 404 or 410 → out. |

`matched_job_title` and `matched_location` list **every** profile entry that matched (not just the first).

## Known bugs in v1 (deliberately broken)

- `resolve_job_town` does only exact-string lookup against a small hardcoded UK TOWNS dict — most jobs fail as `UNKNOWN_LOCATION`. Location extraction should look at multiple page fields and handle multi-location strings.
- `matched_titles` in `match_jobs.py` uses substring containment (`t in job_title`) — the actual rule is every word of the profile title must appear in the job title.
- `matched_locations` passes bare town name to `towns_covered` but profile location `includes` is a list of strings — the towns_covered logic itself is correct, but the job's resolved `town` may not align with what profiles list.
- Company matching is exact string equality against `scraped.company` only — the real rule requires fuzzy matching across multiple page signals.

## Data

- `data/jobs_raw.jsonl` — ~1,500 raw jobs; each has `job_id`, `scraped` (title/company/location/salary), `source_url`, `page` (http_status, title_tag, h1, meta, visible_text, structured_job)
- `data/user_search_inputs/profile_a/` — the recruiter profile (company_searches.json, job_title_searches.json, location_searches.json)
- `data/labelled_sample.jsonl` — 60 hand-labelled jobs; the only ground truth available locally
- `data/golden/` — tiny fixture used by the golden test; must keep passing

## Задача

### Контекст
Рекрутер задаёт поисковые параметры в `data\user_search_inputs`:
- **Компании** — карьерные страницы которых нужно искать (например, Deloitte)
- **Должности** — которые нужно искать (например, Senior Consultant)
- **Локации** — где нужно найти вакансии (например, United Kingdom)

### Суть задачи
Нужно сопоставить 1 500 реальных вакансий из `data\jobs_raw.jsonl` с этими поисковыми параметрами. Этот процесс стоит после скрапинга карьерных страниц — все данные локальные, живые запросы **не требуются**.

Мы предоставили версию 1 в `v1\workers\job_matcher` — базовый каркас для старта, однако он намеренно сломан и точно не сопоставляет вакансии. Подробнее — в README.

Рекрутеры получают комиссию 15–30% от зарплаты: отправить кандидата на позицию £100K — это £15–30K для рекрутингового агентства. В рекрутинге критична скорость — карьерные страницы публикуют вакансии раньше, чем они появляются на LinkedIn, Indeed, Reed и т.д. Успешный скрапинг и точная фильтрация создают сильные лиды для рекрутеров.

### Что оценивается
Цель — создать систему, которая совпадает с ответами нашего производственного job_matcher на ≥ 90% на приватном датасете.

Важнее результата — **процесс**:
- Чистый, лаконичный код: небольшое, хорошо ограниченное решение с явными компромиссами лучше большого
- Эффективность: учитывайте сложность по времени и памяти — должно обрабатывать 200 000 вакансий за 20 минут
- Хорошо написанные тесты для реализованных правил и логики
- Процесс: коммиты часто и понемногу — важно видеть хронологию

Предполагается использование AI-инструментов, но `PLAN.md`, `DECISIONS.md` и `NOTES.md` должны быть написаны лаконично и своими словами.

---

## Система сборки

### Правила сопоставления
- Сопоставление бинарное: вакансия попадает в список только если совпадают все три — компания, хотя бы одна должность, хотя бы одна локация
- Точность важнее объёма — главная ценность продукта в отсутствии шума
- Вакансия в нескольких местах проходит, если хотя бы одно совпадает: «Bristol, Manchester» при поиске по «Bristol» — это проход
- Компания должна быть где-то на странице вакансии (указанная компания, заголовок, title tag, URL или текст страницы) — это лишь слабая проверка, что мы на правильной карьерной странице
- Рекрутеру нужно подтверждение, что вакансия активна. Битая ссылка (404/410) никогда не попадает в список
- Полные определения: [OUTPUT_FORMAT.json](OUTPUT_FORMAT.json)

### Технические предпочтения
- API LLM будет предоставлен, см. `.env.example`. Это живые вызовы с ограниченным бюджетом — **цель £1, максимум £3**
- Использование LLM — на ваше усмотрение, но учитывайте стоимость по сравнению с кодом
- Должно работать на 200 000 вакансий за 20 минут
- `tools/make_scale_feed.py` генерирует тестовый датасет 200 000 вакансий из `data/jobs_raw.jsonl`
- Скрапинг не выполняется — каждая вакансия уже содержит страницу, которую мы скачали единожды: `page.http_status` и всё что она показала. В данных есть заблокированные страницы, битые ссылки, пустые локации, несоответствия заголовков, неверные компании. Также японские символы в локациях и плейсхолдеры вида «3 Locations» — каждый случай требует обоснованной политики обработки

### 4 фазы (1–2 часа суммарно, без бонусов за превышение)

| Фаза | Время | Результат |
|------|-------|-----------|
| Plan | 15–30 мин | `PLAN.md` — написанный вручную |
| Build | 15–30 мин | коммиты |
| Tune | 15–30 мин | коммиты |
| Complete | 15–30 мин | `NOTES.md` |

Записывайте старт и конец в `NOTES.md`, каждое решение — в `DECISIONS.md` по ходу работы. Коммиты — часто и понемногу, не одним разом в конце.

---

## Входные данные

Все входные данные находятся в `data\`.

### Поисковые параметры
Каждый рекрутер имеет папку в `data\user_search_inputs\` (например, `profile_a`) с тремя файлами:
- `company_searches.json` — компании (поле `industry` — только контекст, заполнено примерно наполовину)
- `job_title_searches.json` — должности
- `location_searches.json` — локации с полями: name, country, type и список `includes`

Типы локаций:
- `city` — покрывает своё название и все города из `includes`
- `sub_region` (регион, страна или округ) — покрывает любой город внутри него
- `remote` — покрывает вакансии, где работодатель указывает удалённую/домашнюю работу в этой стране; но вакансия в другой стране никогда не попадает в локацию, как бы город ни назывался

Каждый файл содержит одинаковый `profile_id`, который проставляется на каждой строке вывода. Runtime читает папку через `load_search_inputs` в `v1\shared\patterns\worker_runtime.py`. Оценка производится на другом профиле рекрутера — ничего не должно быть захардкожено под `profile_a`.

### Вакансии
`data\jobs_raw.jsonl` — около 1 500 вакансий, по одной на строку. Каждая содержит:
- `job_id` — копировать в вывод без изменений
- поля `scraped` — title, company, location, salary (часто сокращённые, пустые или неверные)
- `source_url` — анонимизирован, не откроется
- `page` — страница, скачанная единожды: `http_status`, title tag, h1, meta-теги, видимый текст и `structured_job` (факты о вакансии, задекларированные самой страницей: title, company, locations). Любое из этих полей может отсутствовать

### Ответы и тесты
`data\labelled_sample.jsonl` — 60 вакансий с правильным решением (matched_company, matched_job_title, matched_location, reason) — единственный доступный ключ ответов. `data\golden\` — маленький датасет, который уже проходит стартовый код; запускается через `make test`.
